question.text: Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund is being set up in GIFT-IFSC as a Category III AIF, registering as an FPI under SEBI (FPI) Regulations 2019, with a resident Indian manager or sponsor. What is the mandatory sponsor commitment in the fund for this Cat III AIF-FPI?

answer.text: 2.5% of corpus or USD 750,000, whichever is lower
5% of corpus or USD 1.5 million, whichever is lower
10% of corpus or USD 5 million, whichever is lower
No sponsor commitment required for IFSC-domiciled AIFs

explanation.text: The Logic: An IFSC-domiciled Category III AIF registering as an FPI with a resident Indian manager or sponsor must have a Sponsor Commitment of 5% of corpus OR USD 1.5 million, whichever is LOWER. Category I/II in IFSC carries the lower 2.5% or USD 750,000 (whichever lower) commitment. The Trap: Option A is the Category I/II figure. Option C is invented. Option D is wrong because the sponsor commitment is mandatory for IFSC AIF-FPIs. Note: The USD cap often binds before the 5% of corpus calculation for large IFSC funds, so commitment sizing is typically driven by the dollar floor.
